title: Phased Adoption Cost-Latency Notebook
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight working notebook for mapping phased adoption cohorts against the cost vs latency tradeoffs we need to make during rollout. Not meant to be final — experiment notes, quick sims, and an operational checklist to guide the first 90 days of an activation.

Quick summary (TL;DR):
- We propose 4 phasing cohorts (Internal -> Pilot A -> Pilot B -> General Availability).
- For each cohort we outline target requests/day, SLO (p95 latency), preferred deployment mode (hosted/dedicated), and a preferred fallback policy.
- Key decision levers: batching window, quantization/config profile, prefix caching, and region routing.
- Primary KPIs to watch: p95 latency, cost per 1k tokens, error rate, KV cache hit rate, and throughput headroom.

Background context and constraints:
- Product asks for < 300ms p95 on conversational flows for paying cohorts. Non-paying cohorts can tolerate 700ms p95.
- Expected token profile (median): 12 input tokens + 48 generated tokens per request (60 total).
- Baseline hosted cost: $0.40 per 1k output tokens (current pricing experiment). Dedicated unit economics can be ~40% lower at scale for steady-state traffic but requires commit.
- Sequence-length sensitivity: longer contexts (>=512) increase per-token latency non-linearly due to kv-cache and attention kernel behavior.

Phased Adoption Plan (backstop numbers):
1) Internal dogfood (week 0-2)
   - target: 100 daily requests (devs + SEs)
   - mode: hosted (fastest onboarding), can tolerate >=400ms p95 while we validate prompts
   - cost impact: negligible; focus on instrumentation (latency traces, token breakdown)
   - checklist: flagging telemetry, enable debug traces for 10% of requests

2) Pilot A (week 3-6) - Early customers (closed)
   - target: 2k daily requests (avg 50 reqs/min during business hours)
   - SLO: p95 <= 350ms
   - preferred mode: hosted (tiered model with caching and aggressive batching up to 40ms window)
   - config levers: enable prefix caching for top-20 prompts, quantize model to 4-bit if latency regressions acceptable
   - fallback: route to smaller model variant with higher hallucination guard if latency > 600ms
3) Pilot B (week 7-12) - Expanded cohort
   - target: 20k daily requests
   - SLO: p95 <= 300ms (paying users)
   - preferred mode: Dedicated reserved pool (commit conversation GPU pool with autoscale buffer + hosted overflow)
   - capacity plan: reserve capacity for baseline 25 rps sustained; allow hosted burst to 75 rps for spikes
   - cost delta: dedicated expected to reduce per-token cost ~35% vs hosted for this workload
4) GA (post-week 12)
   - target: 200k daily requests (growth dependent)
   - SLOs: p95 <= 300ms for enterprise tier; p95 <= 450ms for free tier
   - mode: hybrid (dedicated regional pools + global hosted fallback)
   - routing: geographic affinity + cost-routing policy to lower-cost regions when latency within tolerance

Sizing / quick sims (assumptions):
- Avg tokens per request = 60; tokens per 1k = 0.06 requests per 1k tokens -> cost per request hosted = 60/1000 * $0.40 = $0.024 per request.
- Pilot B (20k/day) cost hosted = 20k * $0.024 = $480/day -> ~ $14.4k/month.
- If dedicated reduces unit cost by 35%, monthly saves ~ $5k at this scale.
- Important: caching can reduce generated tokens by X% depending on prompt structure; 20-35% reduction materially changes the numbers above.

Operational checklist (pre-phase flip):
- Observability: token-level cost metrics wired to product dashboard, p95 by route, KV cache hit rate, batching seconds distribution (histogram), model fallback counts.
- Runbook: define steps for (a) reducing batch window, (b) disabling quantization, (c) draining regional pool and shifting traffic.
- Guardrails: abnormally high cost alert (> 40% spike MoM) and p95 SLO breach alert (automated rollback to previous model).
- Security/compliance: ensure any Pilot customers with regulated data are mapped to Private deployment or VPC routing (eng-security signoff).

Decision matrix (how we choose mode / levers):
- If target cohort p95 <= 350ms and sustained > 5k daily requests -> consider dedicated.
- If burstiness ratio (peak/sustained) > 4x -> keep hosted fallback enabled.
- If median token length > 128 -> prefer more conservative batching and disable aggressive quantization unless validated.

KPI tracking (minimum):
- p95 latency by route (daily) - target per cohort
- cost per active user (monthly) - include tokens + infra overhead allocation
- KV cache hit rate (hourly) - target > 30% after prompt-optimizations
- batch wait time median (ms) - target < 45ms for low-latency cohorts
- fallback rate (percent of requests hitting fallback) - target < 1% for paying cohorts

Open questions / research spikes (TODO):
- Run short A/B: 4-bit quantization vs 8-bit at Pilot A traffic for hallucination delta. Owner: Sanjay (PRODOPS-742).
- Benchmark prefix-caching delta for our top 10 prompt patterns; estimate token savings. Owner: Maya.
- Simulate regional routing cost tradeoff with realistic spike profiles (tilt at 3x, 6x, 10x). Owner: Tom.

Mini playbook for a sudden SLO breach (working draft):
1) Pager triggers on p95 > 450ms for paying cohort (15m sustained).
2) Product ops: escalate and toggle canary -> reduce batching window by 50% for 50% of traffic.
3) If no improvement in 10 minutes: flip to fallback model variant for new requests and enable hosted overflow.
4) Notify customers in Pilot A slack channel and open incident ticket linking the telemetry snapshot.

Notes / scratch area (raw thoughts):
- If caching reduces generated token length by 25% we shave ~6 cents/request in some scenarios (recompute numbers when we have real samples).
- Consider offering a cheaper "latency-relaxed" plan that routes to quantized model variant and accepts 20% higher fallback rate but halves cost.
- Need a clean way to show customers the cost-latency tradeoff on billing page (visual slider).

Immediate next steps (this week):
- Sanjay: run quantization A/B on staging with 2k simulated RPS trace (due 2025-01-20).
- Maya: extract top-30 prompt templates and estimate prefix-sharing opportunities (due 2025-01-22).
- Tom: build quick cost-vs-region sim notebook (due 2025-01-24).
- Aisha: wire the KPI list to the product-ops dashboard and create the first-run alerts (due 2025-01-28).

Slack channels and references: #prodops-rollouts, #pilot-customer-ops, incident runbook (Confluence link above).

End notes: this doc will be iterated against the Pilot learnings. Keep lightweight. Mark important decisions into Confluence when they exceed a policy threshold (e.g., commit to Dedicated).
